newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL-PROUD CANADIENS TOP DEVILS IN TRIPLE OVERTIME TO AVOID SWEEP.
newsitem.headline: NHL-PROUD CANADIENS TOP DEVILS IN TRIPLE OVERTIME TO AVOID SWEEP.

text.p: Patrice Brisebois chipped a backhander past Martin Brodeur at 7:37 of triple overtime as the Montreal Canadiens sidestepped a playoff sweep with a gutsy 4-3 victory over the New Jersey Devils on Thursday.

Montreal, getting a brilliant effort from rookie goalie Jose Theodore, avoided being swept out of the playoffs on home ice for the first time in 68 years by drawing within 3-1 in their best-of-seven Eastern Conference first-round series.
Brisebois, who missed the first two games of the series with a rib injury, converted on a give-and-go with Saku Koivu.

Koivu slid a pass from the goal line just under a sliding Steve Thomas. Brisebois corraled it with his left skate and flipped a backhander that hopped over Brodeur's right pad for his fourth career post-season goal on the game's 100th shot.
Canadiens coach Mario Tremblay, who had guaranteed a victory, gambled with a surprise move by replacing a shaky Jocelyn Thibault in the nets with rookie Theodore.
Theodore made it pay off by stopping 56 shots, four short of the team playoff record.

"We knew Theodore was going to play yesterday, but kept it secret to keep the pressure off him," said Montreal right winger Mark Recchi, who scored twice for the Canadiens. "We got some great saves from Theodore."
Brodeur finished with 37 saves for the Devils.

New Jersey outshot Montreal in the three overtime periods, 28-16, and nearly won it seconds before Brisebois' goal when Shawn Chambers' shot from the right point glanced off the outside of the right goalpost.
The fifth game of the series will be played Saturday at New Jersey.

Former Canadien Lyle Odelein scored with 96 seconds left in the third period to send the game to overtime. His one-time slapper from the top of the right circle beat Theodore to the stick side, just inside the right goalpost.

At Colorado, Patrick Roy became the most successful goalie in playoff history with his second shutout of the series and Valeri Kamensky scored three power-play goals and set up another as the Avalanche buried the Chicago Blackhawks 7-0.
The victory gave the defending Stanley Cup champions a 3-2 lead in their Western Conference playoff series.
Roy made 25 saves for his 10th career playoff shutout and 89th post-season victory, moving one ahead of Billy Smith, who had 88 wins for the New York Islanders in the 1980s.

"It's a great honour, it's nice to pass a guy like Billy Smith who had a fantastic playoff career," Roy said. "To me it was more important to focus first on the game than focus on that record. Hopefully, I'm going to pass it by two in Chicago in the next game."
Roy preserved the shutout with a pair of breakaway saves in the third period. He stopped James Black 5:20 into the period and stoned Tony Amonte 96 seconds later.
Colorado can wrap up the series Saturday with a victory in Game Six at Chicago.
Kamensky recorded his first career post-season hat trick and Peter Forbserg and Joe Sakic set up three scores apiece for the Avalanche, who registered five power-play goals on 12 opportunities.
"If you play your best against them, you have a chance, and we didn't play our best against them," Chicago coach Craig Hartsburg said. "They played their best, but we didn't."

In Anaheim, Keith Tkachuk scored his fourth and fifth goals of the series and Bob Corkum added a goal and two assists as the Phoenix Coyotes moved within one win of the Western Conference semifinals with a 5-2 win over the Mighty Ducks.
The Coyotes have won the last three games for a 3-2 lead in the best-of-seven series, which resumes Sunday in Phoenix.
Jeremy Roenick and Teppo Numminen scored in a 1:55 span of the second period to break a 1-1 tie.
Teemu Selanne had both goals for the Ducks, whose 16-game home unbeaten streak was snapped.
Tkachuk and Selanne traded first-period goals before Jeremy Roenick put Phoenix ahead for good at 7:17 of the second.
The Ducks outshot Phoenix 32-24, but Nikolai Khabibulin made 30 saves. Selanne's rebound goal with 2:23 to go in the opening period broke Khabibulin's shutout streak at 118 minutes, 48 seconds.
